answers.reasoning: A selector returning a fresh array every call (Object.keys) breaks Object.is on every getSnapshot re-check, so React loops without any actual store change.
v4's useSyncExternalStoreWithSelector memoized the selection per raw snapshot; zustand/traditional's createWithEqualityFn restores that.
useShallow wraps the selector and returns the previous ref via a ref cache when shallow(prev,next) holds, so the outer Object.is check passes.
shallow is one level deep with Object.is per value: nuts/honey unchanged so A keeps its old array, but treats got a new object reference so B re-renders.

Plain zustand has no per-field access tracking; an identity selector subscribes to the whole state object, and set() rebuilds that container on any field change, so it re-renders (but only once, not a loop, since the reference is stable until the next set).
